Yes: the transport cycle of 2026-09-12 (design/cycles/2026-09-12-transport-below-the-boundary.md:703-745). It came to the same answer you just gave: 'keep the signature on the row', about 88 characters a row, and later tied to decision 0009 (the log is what a person's manifestation is formed from, so provenance is everything). What's NEW since then is sealing (cycle 10, 2026-09-23). That plan assumed the row's text is what was signed. Since sealing, the signature covers the sealed, encrypted text, not the opened text the log keeps. So the old plan, 'from + text + sig', would no longer verify. The row also needs the sealed text, as I said above. That's the one thing to add to the old decision; the rest stands.

Landed: jobs.list is now jobs.search plus jobs.get (without the watcher's file list; fileCount stays), and fs.search {q} is new, with its pattern cleaned by fsPath and '../' refused as 'path outside the run folder'. It walks the watcher's servable list, and links aren't followed. Commit 977b02f4. Your tests: the path-cleaning and ../ cases we agreed, and jobs.get on the watcher staying under the cap. Note: the SSE 'snapshot' still pushes every job whole, including the 42 KB file list, to each page. That's local, page-bound, not a verb; worth its own row? Next: peer.list becomes contact.search/get, with contacts.js and contactsDetails.js.

Yes, I agree, and it settles the database decision you deferred until the log could prove its promises: R16 provides the proof, so both go together. Today the log is one append-only file that every read scans whole (trafficLog.js); a table in node.db can be searched by peer, hash or time without reading everything. Go = R16 is built as a node.db table: every traffic row keeps the signature AND the sealed text it covers, the existing traffic.jsonl is imported once, and the readers switch over. It's a core change (a new persist shape), so claude-windows brings the table shape for my review before any code, then it comes back to you. No = the log stays a file, and R16 adds the two fields to each line.

Designed, not lost, but it sat. The 2026-09-12 cycle wrote down what it takes, and R16 has been on the board as owed ever since, which is where you found it. What went wrong is quieter: (1) nobody picked it up, because nothing was declared as waiting on it, although your database decision was; (2) when sealing arrived on 09-23 it changed R16's premise (the signed bytes became the sealed text), and nobody updated R16's text to say so; (3) my own test for it looked at the wrong file and couldn't have noticed it being built (fixed today, 78f0ecb). So the plan survived; the connection to the database decision and the sealing change didn't. The Go/No I just sent you puts both back together.

One choice before peer.list becomes contact.search, because it changes your Contacts screen. Each row today shows a mark: blocked, or waiting for you to accept. A search answers key/label pairs only, so the mark needs a home. (a) RECOMMENDED: it goes into the label as a word, e.g. 'Bert — blocked', 'Carol — waiting'. One request, the table still shows it, and searching 'blocked' or 'waiting' lists exactly those people, which is new. (b) The mark shows only when you open a person (contact.get), and the table is names only. Go! = (a). No = (b).
